the liver plays a minor role in the metabolism of sex steroids in patients with alcoholic cirrhotic liver.
sex steroids in men are cleared by the liver, but that this clearance depends on the degree of hepatic function impairment and on the binding affinity of sex steroid binding globulin.
the hepatic clearance of sex steroids is influenced by liver function, but that the circulating levels are influenced by the production rate and peripheral metabolism, as well as the hepatic uptake.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sex steroids may have a role in the pathophysiology of alcoholic cirrhosis, and that the altered sex steroid levels may contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease.
liver function impairment may affect the hepatic clearance of steroids in alcoholic cirrhoses.
